Ben & Jerry’s
Public-information pitch deck test
A realistic investor-style deck built from public facts so Zelda can test extraction, Truth Delta, memo grounding, and private/public-company presentation logic.
TEST ARTIFACT — NOT OFFICIAL
CLAIMS DESIGNED FOR VERIFICATION
Prepared for Interlink Foundry / Zelda Intelligence QA

Why this deck exists
A deliberately “realistic but testable” public-company-style deck.
Purpose
• Give Zelda a clean second benchmark after Nike: recognizable brand, many public sources, but not a public standalone issuer.
• Test whether Truth Delta separates brand facts, parent-company facts, mission claims, market context, and unsupported deck claims.
• Create extraction targets across history, ownership, operating model, distribution, values, risks, and strategic narrative.
Expected Zelda behavior: verify public facts, downgrade context-only claims, and label unsupported or forward-looking assertions without treating them as proven.
Synthetic public-information deck for Zelda testing • Not an official Ben & Jerry’s deck

Company snapshot
Iconic super-premium ice cream brand with unusually explicit social mission positioning.
1978
Founded in Burlington, Vermont
2000
Acquired by Unilever
3-part
Product, economic, social mission
Core positioning
Premium indulgence + playful flavor innovation + activist brand values. Ben & Jerry’s publicly frames the business around “linked prosperity,” where product quality, sustainable growth, and social mission should thrive together.
Zelda extraction targets
founded year
ownership
mission
strategy
Sources: Ben & Jerry’s values page; Unilever public pages.
Synthetic public-information deck for Zelda testing • Not an official Ben & Jerry’s deck

Origin story & brand equity
From Vermont scoop shop to global cultural brand.
Brand-building pattern
• Small-company origin gives the brand authenticity that still differentiates it inside a large CPG portfolio.
• Flavor naming, mix-ins, and cause-linked campaigns create social shareability beyond product taste alone.
• The brand is unusually transparent about values, making mission a feature of the product experience.
Investor-style thesis
Ben & Jerry’s is not merely selling ice cream; it is monetizing a high-affinity brand community around indulgence, identity, and values.
Sources: Ben & Jerry’s values/mission public pages.

Product engine
High-recognition flavors, seasonal innovation, and scoop-shop experience create multiple demand surfaces.
Revenue surfaces to identify
Retail pints
Grocery / freezer aisle distribution
Scoop shops
On-premise experience and franchise/local retail
Limited flavors
Innovation-driven demand spikes
Activism-led drops
Earned-media amplification when credible
Deck claim to test
“Ben & Jerry’s flavor innovation and mission-led campaigns create earned-media advantages versus generic premium ice cream.”
Synthetic public-information deck for Zelda testing • Not an official Ben & Jerry’s deck

Market & distribution context
The brand benefits from parent-scale cold chain and a global ice cream category backdrop.
€7.9B
Unilever ice cream unit 2024 sales reported by Reuters
~20%
Share of global ice cream market reported for the unit
Important distinction
These are parent/ice-cream-unit figures, not standalone Ben & Jerry’s revenue. A good diligence system should not assign them directly to the brand without segment-level disclosure.
Truth Delta trap
Deck includes parent-unit metrics beside brand narrative so Zelda can test attribution boundaries.
Source: Reuters report on Unilever ice cream spin-off.
Synthetic public-information deck for Zelda testing • Not an official Ben & Jerry’s deck

Mission as strategic asset
Ben & Jerry’s makes social mission part of the brand promise, not a side program.
Publicly stated core values
Human rights & dignity
Freedom, security, self-esteem, expression, protest.
Social & economic justice
Equity, opportunity, justice, fair livelihoods.
Environmental restoration
Positive, life-giving impact and restoration of natural systems.
Strategic upside: values sharpen differentiation. Strategic risk: activism can create governance and distribution friction.
Source: Ben & Jerry’s values page.
Synthetic public-information deck for Zelda testing • Not an official Ben & Jerry’s deck

Ownership & governance context
A strong mission-led brand inside a large parent structure can create both scale and tension.
Known public context
• Ben & Jerry’s was acquired by Unilever in 2000, with public reporting emphasizing continued brand mission and independent board issues.
• Unilever announced plans to separate its ice cream business into The Magnum Ice Cream Company; reporting described Ben & Jerry’s as part of that unit.
• Public reporting has described tensions between Ben & Jerry’s social mission independence and parent-company governance.
Zelda challenge
Separate settled historical facts from current-state corporate events that may have changed after source publication.
Sources: Unilever public pages; Reuters/AP public reporting.
Synthetic public-information deck for Zelda testing • Not an official Ben & Jerry’s deck

Risks & diligence questions
The brand is valuable, but the operating model has real diligence questions.
Attribution risk
Brand-level revenue and margin may not be separately disclosed.
Governance risk
Mission independence can conflict with parent-level risk management.
Category risk
Frozen desserts require cold-chain execution and face private-label pressure.
Reputation risk
Activism creates loyalty with some consumers and backlash with others.
Verification risk
Some claims are mission narrative, not measurable operating data.
Core diligence question: Can Ben & Jerry’s preserve brand-led pricing power and cultural relevance while operating inside a scaled global ice cream company?
Synthetic public-information deck for Zelda testing • Not an official Ben & Jerry’s deck
